Example pinyin: Qǐngwèn, cèsuǒ zài nǎr?

Example (EN): Hello, my name is Anna.

Example (EN): Thank you for your help.

Example (Traditional): 不客氣，這是我應該做的。
Example pinyin: Bù kèqi, zhè shì wǒ yīnggāi zuò de.
Example (EN): You're welcome, it was the least I could do.

Example pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ lái wǎn le.
Example (EN): Sorry, I'm late.

Example (EN): It's fine, don't worry.
Notes: The usual reply to 对不起.

Example pinyin: Qǐngwèn, dìtiězhàn zěnme zǒu?
Example (EN): Excuse me, how do I get to the subway station?
Notes: Polite way to start a question to a stranger.

Example pinyin: Zhège duōshao qián?
Example (EN): How much is this?

Example pinyin: Tài guì le, piányi yīdiǎn ba.
Example (EN): That's too expensive, can you make it a bit cheaper?
Notes: Useful for bargaining at markets.

Example pinyin: Zhè jiā fànguǎn hěn piányi.
Example (EN): This restaurant is cheap.

Example pinyin: Yī píng shuǐ sān kuài qián.
Example (EN): A bottle of water costs three yuan.
Notes: 元 (yuán) is the written/formal form; 块 is also a measure word for pieces.

Example pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ tīng bu dǒng Zhōngwén.
Example (EN): Sorry, I don't understand spoken Chinese.
Notes: 看不懂 (kàn bu dǒng) = can't understand something written.

Example (Simplified): 请说慢一点，我是外国人。
Example (Traditional): 請說慢一點，我是外國人。
Example pinyin: Qǐng shuō màn yīdiǎn, wǒ shì wàiguórén.
Example (EN): Please speak more slowly, I'm a foreigner.

Example pinyin: Jiùmìng! Yǒu rén diào jìn shuǐ li le!
Example (EN): Help! Someone has fallen into the water!
Notes: Only for real emergencies.

Example pinyin: Nǐ zhù zài nǎr?
Example (EN): Where are you staying?
Notes: Northern usage; 哪里 (nǎlǐ) is common in the south and Taiwan.

Example pinyin: Qiánmiàn lùkǒu wǎng zuǒ guǎi.
Example (EN): Turn left at the intersection ahead.

Example pinyin: Yínháng zài yòubian.
Example (EN): The bank is on the right.

Example pinyin: Yīzhí zǒu, ránhòu wǎng yòu guǎi.
Example (EN): Go straight, then turn right.

Example pinyin: Wǒmen zuò dìtiě qù ba.
Example (EN): Let's take the subway.
Notes: In Taiwan the metro is called 捷运 (jiéyùn).

Example pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ jiào yī liàng chūzūchē.
Example (EN): Please call a taxi for me.
Notes: 打车 (dǎchē) = to take a taxi. Taiwan: 计程车 (jìchéngchē).

Example pinyin: Huǒchēzhàn lí zhèr yuǎn ma?
Example (EN): Is the train station far from here?

Example pinyin: Wǒ yào qù jīchǎng.
Example (EN): I need to go to the airport.

Example pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi liǎng zhāng piào.
Example (EN): I'd like to buy two tickets.

Example (Traditional): 這輛公交車去火車站嗎？
Example pinyin: Zhè liàng gōngjiāochē qù huǒchēzhàn ma?
Example (EN): Does this bus go to the train station?
Notes: Taiwan: 公车 (gōngchē).

Example pinyin: Fúwùyuán, qǐng gěi wǒ càidān.
Example (EN): Waiter, could I have the menu, please?

Example pinyin: Fúwùyuán, mǎidān!
Example (EN): Waiter, the bill please!
Notes: 结账 (jiézhàng) is also common.

Example pinyin: Zhège cài bùyào là, xièxie.
Example (EN): No chili in this dish, please.
Notes: 微辣 (wēilà) = mildly spicy.

Example pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī bēi shuǐ.
Example (EN): Please give me a glass of water.
Notes: 热水 (rèshuǐ) = hot water; 冰水 (bīngshuǐ) = iced water.

Example pinyin: Zhège jiǎozi hěn hǎochī.
Example (EN): These dumplings are delicious.

Example (Simplified): 我要这个，再要一碗米饭。
Example (Traditional): 我要這個，再要一碗米飯。
Example pinyin: Wǒ yào zhège, zài yào yī wǎn mǐfàn.
Example (EN): I'll have this, and a bowl of rice as well.
Notes: Handy when pointing at a menu picture.

Example pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn hěn gānjìng.
Example (EN): This hotel is very clean.
Notes: Also 宾馆 (bīnguǎn); in Taiwan often 饭店 (fàndiàn).

Example pinyin: Wǒ dìngle yī gè fángjiān.

Example (EN): I booked the room online.

Example pinyin: Wǒ de fángjiān yàoshi diū le.
Example (EN): I've lost my room key.
Notes: Hotels often use a key card: 房卡 (fángkǎ).

Example pinyin: Zuìjìn de yīyuàn zài nǎr?
Example (EN): Where is the nearest hospital?
Notes: Mainland emergency ambulance number: 120.

Example pinyin: Zhège yào yī tiān chī sān cì.
Example (EN): Take this medicine three times a day.
Notes: 药店 (yàodiàn) = pharmacy. Chinese "eats" medicine (吃药).

Example pinyin: Kuài jiào jǐngchá!

Example (EN): I'm sick and need to go to the hospital.

Example pinyin: Wǒ dùzi hěn téng.
Example (EN): My stomach really hurts.

English: to help, to do a favour

Example (EN): Thanks for helping!

Example pinyin: Xiànzài jǐ diǎn?
Example (EN): What time is it now?

Example pinyin: Huǒchē zǎoshang bā diǎn kāi.
Example (EN): The train leaves at eight in the morning.

Example pinyin: Jīntiān wǒmen qù Chángchéng.
Example (EN): Today we're going to the Great Wall.

Example pinyin: Míngtiān jiàn!
Example (EN): See you tomorrow!

Example pinyin: Wǒ yào liǎng píng píjiǔ.
Example (EN): I'd like two bottles of beer.
Notes: Use 两 before a measure word; use 二 (èr) when counting or in numbers like 十二.

Example pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu liǎng bǎi kuài.
Example (EN): This item of clothing is 200 yuan.

English: to pay by card, swipe a card
Example pinyin: Kěyǐ shuākǎ ma?
Example (EN): Can I pay by card?
Notes: In mainland China mobile payment (扫码 sǎomǎ, scanning a QR code) is far more common.

Example pinyin: Zàijiàn, lùshang xiǎoxīn!

Example pinyin: Wǒ mílù le, nǐ néng bāng wǒ ma?

Example (EN): I go to archery every weekend.

Example pinyin: Tā shèle liù zhī jiàn.

Example (EN): The bowstring broke, so I need a new one.

Example (EN): A finger tab protects your fingers.

Example pinyin: Jiàntóu chā zài bǎzi shang.
Example (EN): The arrowhead is stuck in the target.

Example pinyin: Zhè zhī jiàn de jiànyǔ huài le.
Example (EN): The fletching on this arrow is damaged.

Example pinyin: Tànsù jiàngǎn yòu qīng yòu zhí.
Example (EN): Carbon arrow shafts are light and straight.

Example (EN): You shoot really accurately!

Example (EN): The distance for indoor competitions is 18 metres.

Example (EN): In archery, safety comes first.

Example (EN): People who aren't shooting stay behind the waiting line.

Example (EN): Never dry-fire: it can break the bow.
